The zero-g indicator on Crew-13 (and every crewed Dragon flight) is the usual soft plush the crew picks. It stays a surprise until it starts floating on the live feed after they reach orbit.Crew-13 is launching today (Oct 1, 2026) at 11:10 a.m. EDT on Dragon Grace from SLC-40, with NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins (commander) and Luke Delaney (pilot), CSA astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov. The indicator is tethered in the cabin so it hangs during the boost phase and lifts off once the engines cut and they’re in free fall. Because the crew is locked into harnesses, that floating toy is the clear visual cue they’ve hit microgravity—tradition that goes back at least to Yuri Gagarin’s little doll on Vostok 1.Crews keep the choice secret until roughly 10–30 minutes after liftoff, when it appears on the broadcast. Past Dragon examples include:Demo-2: sequined dinosaur “Tremor” 
Crew-1: Grogu plush 
Crew-2: penguin “GuinGuin” 
Crew-3: turtle “Pfau” 
Crew-10: hand-crocheted origami crane “друг” (Droog, “friend”) 
Polaris Dawn: Shiba Inu plush named Asteroid 
 
Watch the SpaceX/NASA stream after SECO for today’s reveal.

American Idiot is a community project built on punk spirit, satire, and independent thought. The A in American and the I in Idiot spell AI, turning our name into a question: as machines get smarter, are humans becoming more willing to stop thinking?
We stand against AI making humanity dumber—against outsourcing judgment to algorithms, treating generated answers as unquestionable truth, and accepting the grand promises of tech companies without scrutiny. AI should expand human ability, while curiosity, creativity, and judgment remain in human hands. Through public topics, the AI Idiot Awards, and the Hall of Idiots, we use humor and satire to challenge AI hype and encourage people to ask their own questions, express their own ideas, and take responsibility for what they believe.
